Acceptance: add the Rule 11 qualifier to the dismissal ground in mechanism (and gather) in both languages, e.g. 'every charge was dismissed (and not as part of a plea agreement in another criminal case under Criminal Rule 11)'. Defect: the packet gives the blanket lead-with-ICHAT instruction that the committed memo's binding packet_instruction for this exact track forbids. MI.memo.json tracks[mi_auto_misd92].legalDesignDecision.limitations: 'Where the participant's only record is a 92-day-or-less misdemeanour that was never fingerprinted to MSP, checking ICHAT proves nothing. Tell them to check with the convicting court. A blanket instruction to lead with the MSP Clean Slate check is wrong for this population.' The committed nextStep.en/es and destination.en/es lead with ICHAT unconditionally ('ICHAT is where you confirm the set-aside actually happened') and no element tells a never-fingerprinted participant that an ICHAT result proves nothing for them; lane B's own evidence record states memo limitations are binding on participant copy and 'followed rather than summarised away'. Acceptance: add the never-fingerprinted caveat and the convicting-court verification path to nextStep/destination/afterNextStep in both languages. Defect: afterNextStep.en/es presents an exhaustive stopper list — 'Three things can stop it' (prior conviction under MCL 28.243(14); objection on a dismissal; records lag) — that omits the other committed exclusion prong of MCL 28.243(14): 'a person arraigned for enumerated offences, including the commission or attempted commission of a crime with or against a child under 16' (MI.memo.json tracks[mi_arrest_acquittal_dismissal].exclusions[0]; the memo also asks participantInput arraignedEnumeratedOffence). gather never asks about it either, so a participant arraigned for an enumerated offence is affirmatively told automatic destruction has only three stoppers and would wrongly expect relief. Same defect class as first-pass F2-01 (committed screen not reaching the participant). Acceptance: add the arraigned-for-enumerated-offence prong to gather and afterNextStep in both languages (and drop or widen the 'three things' count).

Defect: nextSteps.en[2] misstates the age element of the minor-offence definition as 'committed under age 21' (es[2] 'cometidos antes de los 21 años'). The only committed source carrying the test — MI.memo.json controllingAuthority.summary — says 'committed by a person not more than 21 years old', which includes 21-year-olds; the packet's own mechanism.en/es states it correctly ('not more than 21 years old' / 'no más de 21 años'), so the entry contradicts itself and no committed source carries the under-21 formulation. A 21-year-old participant screening with nextSteps would wrongly exclude a qualifying minor offence. Acceptance: change nextSteps item 3 in both languages to 'committed by a person not more than 21 years old' / 'cometidos por una persona de no más de 21 años', matching the memo, the mechanism and authority[2].
